questions.stem: The INDIAN SPACE RESEARCH ORGANISATION (ISRO) was established on:

options.option_text: 15 AUGUST 1969 — superseded INCOSPAR (1962); founded by DR. VIKRAM SARABHAI; HQ Bengaluru

questions.explanation: ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation) — India's national space agency. ESTABLISHED: 15 AUGUST 1969 (Independence Day). REPLACED earlier INCOSPAR (Indian National Committee for Space Research, est. 1962 under Atomic Energy Commission). FOUNDER + FIRST CHAIRMAN: DR. VIKRAM SARABHAI ('Father of Indian Space Programme'); HOMI BHABHA key early backer. HQ: BENGALURU (known as 'Space City'). Governs under DEPARTMENT OF SPACE (DoS), which reports DIRECTLY to the PRIME MINISTER (no separate minister). FIRST ROCKET LAUNCH: Nike-Apache sounding rocket launched 21 NOVEMBER 1963 from THUMBA EQUATORIAL ROCKET LAUNCHING STATION (TERLS), near Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala. PARTS TRANSPORTED on BICYCLE + BULLOCK CART — iconic images. EVOLUTION: (1) 1972 — Dept of Space created. (2) 1975 — ARYABHATA, India's first satellite (launched by USSR Soyuz from Kapustin Yar). (3) 1980 — ROHINI launched by SLV-3 — first INDIGENOUS launch; Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was project director. (4) 1984 — RAKESH SHARMA became FIRST INDIAN in SPACE (aboard Soyuz T-11 with USSR cosmonauts); famously told PM Indira Gandhi 'SARE JAHAN SE ACHCHHA' about India from space. (5) 1988-1993 — Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) development; first success 1994. (6) 2008 — CHANDRAYAAN-1 (first Moon mission; discovered water molecules on Moon). (7) 2013-14 — MARS ORBITER MISSION (MANGALYAAN) — India became FIRST Asian + FIRST country to reach Mars on MAIDEN attempt; Rs. 450 cr budget (cheaper than Hollywood movie 'Gravity'). (8) 2017 — PSLV-C37 launched 104 SATELLITES in single mission (WORLD RECORD). (9) 2019 — CHANDRAYAAN-2 (partial success — orbiter successful, lander Vikram crashed). (10) 2023 — CHANDRAYAAN-3 successful soft-landing near SOUTH POLE of Moon on 23 AUG 2023 — INDIA = FIRST country ever near lunar south pole. (11) 2023 — ADITYA-L1 solar observatory to L1 Lagrange point (reached Jan 2024). (12) 2024 — GAGANYAAN crewed mission prep; TVD-1 abort test. CURRENT CHAIRMAN (2023-): Dr S. SOMANATH (successor to S. Somanath; next in line unclear).

questions.stem: India's first satellite, ARYABHATA, was launched in 1975 by:

options.option_text: USSR (Soviet Union) from KAPUSTIN YAR cosmodrome on 19 April 1975; named after the 5th-century Indian mathematician-astronomer

questions.explanation: ARYABHATA — INDIA's FIRST SATELLITE. LAUNCHED 19 APRIL 1975 from KAPUSTIN YAR cosmodrome (USSR, now Russia) aboard a COSMOS-3M rocket. Indo-Soviet space cooperation. Named after ARYABHATA, the 5th-century Indian mathematician-astronomer (authored Aryabhatiya 499 CE; place-value system). SPECIFICATIONS: ~360 kg; 26-faced polyhedron body; carried 3 experiments — X-ray astronomy, aeronomy (study of upper atmosphere), solar physics. Operated only 4 days before power failure (due to bit error + failure of internal electronics); re-entered atmosphere 11 Feb 1992 after 17 years in orbit. Still considered a major success as it established India's satellite-engineering capability. Design + development at SHAR (Sriharikota HIGH Altitude Range), Peenya, Bengaluru, Thiruvananthapuram. Image of Aryabhata was on INDIAN ₹2 NOTE during 1976-97. SUBSEQUENT EARLY ISRO MISSIONS: (1) 1979 — BHASKARA-I — Earth observation; (2) 1980 — ROHINI (RS-1) — FIRST satellite launched by INDIGENOUS Indian rocket (SLV-3, developed under Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam). India became 7th space-faring nation. (3) 1981 — BHASKARA-II. (4) 1981 — APPLE (Ariane Passenger Payload Experiment) — first 3-axis stabilised communication satellite; launched by ESA Ariane-1. (5) 1982 — INSAT-1A (first Insat). (6) 1983 — INSAT-1B (milestone — communication + weather). (7) 1988 — IRS-1A (Indian Remote Sensing). (8) 1992 — SROSS-C (student satellite). (9) 1993 — PSLV-D1 (failed); 1994 — PSLV-D2 successful. (10) 1999 — GSLV-D1 launched. MILESTONES via PSLV — 58+ LAUNCHES as of 2024 with 95%+ success rate; earned INDIA the 'WORKHORSE LAUNCHER' reputation. PSLV LAUNCHED SATELLITES for 30+ countries (commercial customers) via ANTRIX (ISRO commercial arm), later NSIL (2019). India's per-kg launch cost is AMONG THE LOWEST globally — ~$5000-6000/kg (vs $20000+ for US competitors pre-SpaceX).

questions.stem: CHANDRAYAAN-3, which made INDIA the FIRST COUNTRY to soft-land near the Moon's SOUTH POLE, touched down on:

options.option_text: 23 AUGUST 2023 — 6:04 PM IST; celebrated as NATIONAL SPACE DAY annually since 2023

questions.explanation: CHANDRAYAAN-3 — India's THIRD lunar mission + FIRST successful soft-landing. LAUNCHED: 14 July 2023 on LVM3-M4 from Sriharikota. TOUCH-DOWN: 23 AUGUST 2023 at 6:04 PM IST (Local Indian time 18:04 Hours UTC+5:30). LANDING SITE: Statio Shiv Shakti (later officially named by PM Modi) near Manzinus C and Simpelius N craters, near the Moon's SOUTH POLE (69.37°S, 32.35°E). INDIA BECAME: (1) FOURTH country to soft-land on Moon (after USSR 1966 Luna 9, USA 1966 Surveyor 1, China 2013 Chang'e-3); (2) FIRST country ever to land near the LUNAR SOUTH POLE (Russia's Luna-25 crashed Aug 19, 2023 — failed; Chandrayaan-3 succeeded 4 days later). KEY COMPONENTS: (1) PROPULSION MODULE — orbits Moon; retained in orbit for year+ (SHAPE experiment on it studied Earth as 'habitable' exoplanet-analog). (2) VIKRAM LANDER (~1,752 kg) — named after Vikram Sarabhai; equipped with ChaSTE (thermal), ILSA (seismology), RAMBHA-LP (plasma), LRA (laser retroreflector). (3) PRAGYAN ROVER (~26 kg, 6-wheeled, solar-powered) — deployed from Vikram; traveled ~100m over 14 Earth days on lunar surface; 10-day operational life before lunar night shut it down. Confirmed sulfur, aluminum, calcium, iron, titanium, oxygen, chromium, manganese, silicon on lunar south polar region; temperature measurements by ChaSTE revealed subsurface temperature -10°C. MISSION COST: ₹615 CRORE (~$75 million) — compared with NASA Artemis $4.1 billion. LEADERSHIP: Chairman S. SOMANATH; Project Director P. VEERAMUTHUVEL; Mission Director M. SANKARAN. IMPACT: INDIA celebrated; PM Modi announced 23 Aug as 'NATIONAL SPACE DAY' annually. Worldwide tributes; elevated ISRO's stature. PREVIOUS ATTEMPTS: CHANDRAYAAN-1 (2008) — discovered water ice on Moon (Moon Impact Probe); ended Aug 2009 when communication lost. CHANDRAYAAN-2 (July 2019) — Vikram lander CRASHED (7 Sep 2019) 2km from target; Orbiter (still operational, providing data) was successful. CHANDRAYAAN-3 was REDESIGNED from Chandrayaan-2 lessons — no orbiter (used the CH-2 orbiter), stronger legs, more fuel, hazard detection, multiple backup sensors. FUTURE: CHANDRAYAAN-4 (2027?) — sample return mission; LUPEX (Lunar Polar Exploration) joint with JAXA (Japan).

questions.stem: The MARS ORBITER MISSION (MANGALYAAN) was notable for:

options.option_text: Being the most expensive space mission
Making INDIA the FIRST ASIAN + FIRST COUNTRY EVER to reach Mars ORBIT on MAIDEN ATTEMPT; at under ₹450 cr, cheaper than Hollywood's 'Gravity' ($100M)
Being the first mission to land on Mars

questions.explanation: MARS ORBITER MISSION (MOM) / 'MANGALYAAN' — India's first interplanetary mission. LAUNCHED: 5 NOVEMBER 2013 from Sriharikota on PSLV-C25. ARRIVAL at MARS ORBIT: 24 SEPTEMBER 2014 (after 298-day cruise). KEY ACHIEVEMENTS: (1) INDIA = FIRST ASIAN COUNTRY to reach Mars orbit (Japan Nozomi 1998 + China Yinghuo-1 2011 failed). (2) ISRO = first space agency EVER to achieve Mars orbit on MAIDEN ATTEMPT (USA, Europe, USSR, Japan, China all failed on first attempts). (3) COST: ₹450 CRORE ($73 million) — LOWER COST than the Hollywood movie 'Gravity' ($100M, 2013) — famous cost-comparison point showing Indian frugal engineering. NASA's MAVEN mission to Mars in same window cost $671M. (4) Payloads (5 instruments, 15 kg total): (a) LAP (Lyman Alpha Photometer) — deuterium/hydrogen ratio; (b) MENCA (neutral composition analyzer); (c) Mars Colour Camera (MCC) — stunning Mars + phobos images; (d) TIS (Thermal Infrared Spectrometer); (e) MSM (Methane Sensor). DESIGN LIFE: 6 months; ACTUAL LIFE: 8+ YEARS (ran till 2 October 2022 when contact lost due to eclipse-induced battery drain). NOMINAL 6-month orbit of 366×80000 km. HIGHLIGHTS: (1) Captured iconic 'Full DISK of MARS' with clouds + Olympus Mons visible. (2) Mapped Mars surface; measured atmospheric dust, methane, escape rates. (3) Provided key data for next decade of Mars science. TEAM: Project Director — M. ANNADURAI; ISRO Chairman K. RADHAKRISHNAN. WOMEN SCIENTISTS at MOM: RITU KARIDHAL (Deputy Director Operations), NANDINI HARINATH (deputy operations), MINAL SAMPATH, Anuradha TK — popularised as 'Rocket Women of India'. MOM-2 / MANGALYAAN-2 — in planning for late 2020s; orbiter + possibly lander. NEXT INTERPLANETARY MISSIONS: (1) VENUS ORBITER Mission (Shukrayaan-1) — approved 2024, planned 2028 launch. (2) Space-based Gravitational Wave detector (LISA-India? / LIGO-India Hingoli operational 2030). (3) ADITYA-L1 (ALREADY at L1 Lagrange point since Jan 2024) — first Indian solar observatory. ISRO has 'DRE' culture (Do it Rightful + Efficient + economical) as its famous engineering ethos.

questions.stem: The GAGANYAAN mission, India's first HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT programme, aims to launch Indian astronauts (Vyomanauts) to:

options.option_text: LOW EARTH ORBIT (~400 km) for 3 days — targeted 2025-26; uses LVM3; 4 astronauts selected in 2024 for training

questions.explanation: GAGANYAAN ('Sky Vehicle') — India's first HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT PROGRAMME. Announced 2018 (PM Modi's 15 Aug Independence Day speech). OBJECTIVE: launch 3-member Indian crew to LOW EARTH ORBIT (400 km altitude) for 3 days; safe recovery in Arabian Sea. LAUNCH VEHICLE: LVM3 (previously GSLV Mk-III; HUMAN-RATED variant HLVM3). CREW SELECTION: 4 IAF pilots selected + announced 27 Feb 2024 by PM Modi at ISRO Trivandrum: (1) Group Captain Prashanth Balakrishnan Nair; (2) Group Captain Ajit Krishnan; (3) Group Captain Angad Pratap; (4) Wing Commander Shubhanshu Shukla. ALL 4 undergoing cosmonaut training in ROSCOSMOS (Russia) + in India at Astronaut Training Facility Bengaluru. ONE of them will likely become India's first crewed astronaut via an Indian rocket (RAKESH SHARMA 1984 went via Soviet Soyuz; Gaganyaan will use Indian vehicle). TIMELINE: (1) 21 Oct 2023 — TV-D1 (Test Vehicle Demonstration-1) pad abort test successful; tested Crew Escape System; CES propelled Crew Module from simulated rocket failure at Mach 1.2, 17 km, separated, splashdown in Bay of Bengal. (2) 2024 — G1 uncrewed mission (with humanoid robot VYOMMITRA onboard); delayed to late 2024 / 2025. (3) 2025-26 — G2 uncrewed; then H1 crewed. CURRENT TARGET: H1 crewed mission by 2025/2026. COSTS: ~₹9,000-10,000 CRORE. BUDGET: allocated ₹10,000 cr in 2018. KEY SYSTEMS: (1) CREW MODULE (CM) — re-entry capsule; life support for 3; ~5 tonnes. (2) SERVICE MODULE (SM). (3) CREW ESCAPE SYSTEM (CES) — rockets to pull capsule away from failing booster. (4) Environment Control + Life Support System (ECLSS). POST-Gaganyaan: (a) BHARATIYA ANTARIKSH STATION — India's proposed space station by 2035; first module 2028; (b) Chandrayaan-4 sample return mission (2027); (c) VYOMMITRA Humanoid robot in TV-D1/G1 tests. Gaganyaan will make India the FOURTH country with independent human spaceflight capability after USSR/Russia, USA, China. IAF's INSTITUTE OF AEROSPACE MEDICINE (IAM, Bengaluru) medical + psychological selection. VIKAS ENGINE (2-engine crew version), C-25 cryogenic upper stage, + indigenous pad abort motors developed.

questions.stem: ISRO's WORKHORSE launch vehicle for SMALL + MEDIUM satellites into POLAR ORBIT is:

options.option_text: PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle) — 4-stage rocket, 1994 onward; payload ~1,750 kg to 600 km SSO; holds 104-satellite single-launch record

questions.explanation: PSLV (POLAR SATELLITE LAUNCH VEHICLE) — ISRO's most reliable + workhorse launcher. First launch 1993 (PSLV-D1 failed); first success PSLV-D2 in 1994. 50+ consecutive successful launches since then (as of 2025). STAGES: 4 stages alternating SOLID (PS1, PS3) + LIQUID (PS2, PS4). Payload: ~1,750 kg to SSO (Sun Synchronous Orbit ~620 km), ~1,425 kg to GTO. CONFIGURATIONS: PSLV-CA (Core Alone, no strap-ons), PSLV-DL (2 strap-ons), PSLV-QL (4), PSLV-XL (6) — most powerful. PSLV LAUNCHES: has orbited 400+ satellites from 30+ countries; many commercial launches through ANTRIX / NSIL. RECORD: (1) PSLV-C37 (15 Feb 2017) launched 104 SATELLITES in SINGLE mission — WORLD RECORD at the time (3 Indian satellites + 88 Planet Labs Flock-3p + 1 UAE + 5 Kazakhstan + 5 Switzerland + 1 Israel + 8 Spire Global + 1 UAE); India's primary payload was CARTOSAT-2 series. (2) 2023 — PSLV-C55 launched TeLEOS-2 + Lumelite-4 for Singapore. FAMOUS PSLV MISSIONS: (a) CHANDRAYAAN-1 (2008); (b) MARS ORBITER MISSION (2013); (c) ASTROSAT (2015, India's 1st astronomy satellite); (d) IRNSS / NavIC constellation (PSLV launched 7 IRNSS satellites 2013-16); (e) RISAT (radar imaging); (f) CARTOSAT series (remote sensing); (g) OCEANSAT. OTHER ISRO LAUNCHERS: (1) SLV-3 (1980) — India's 1st indigenous; 40 kg to LEO; 4 missions (2 success, 2 failure); Dr Kalam was project director. (2) ASLV (Augmented SLV, 1987-94) — improvement; 150 kg LEO; 4 missions, 2 success. (3) GSLV Mk-II (2014-present) — 2.5 ton to GTO; uses CRYOGENIC upper stage (CE-7.5, indigenous since 2014). Reliability mixed. (4) GSLV Mk-III / LVM3 (2014-) — HEAVY-LIFT; 4 ton to GTO, 8 ton to LEO; flies LVM3 = Launch Vehicle Mark 3 since 2022 renaming; cryogenic CE-20 upper stage; used for Chandrayaan-2, 3, OneWeb constellation launches (36 OneWeb satellites per launch). HUMAN-RATED for Gaganyaan. (5) SSLV (Small Satellite Launch Vehicle, 2022-) — new; 500 kg to 500 km LEO; designed for rapid commercial small-sat market (SmallSat demand). (6) RLV-TD (Reusable Launch Vehicle Tech Demonstrator) — test flights in 2016, 2023, 2024; technology for Indian reusable rocket.

questions.stem: India's satellite NAVIGATION system (like GPS) is called:

options.option_text: NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) — 7 satellites covering India + 1500 km; official name IRNSS earlier

questions.explanation: NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) — India's regional satellite navigation system. ORIGINAL NAME: IRNSS (Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System). RENAMED NavIC by PM Modi in 2016 post first operational. COVERAGE: India + 1500 km beyond its borders. OWNER + OPERATOR: ISRO. CONSTELLATION: 7 SATELLITES — (1) 3 GEOSTATIONARY (GEO) — at longitudes 32.5°E, 83°E, 131.5°E; (2) 4 GEOSYNCHRONOUS (GSO) — at 55°E + 111.75°E (2 each); inclination 29°. 8TH satellite being built as backup. First satellite IRNSS-1A launched 1 JULY 2013; last of initial 7 IRNSS-1G on 28 APRIL 2016 (making NavIC OPERATIONAL). 7-of-9 launched; 1A failed (atomic clock stopped, replaced 2018 by 1I); 1H also failed in 2017 (heat shield stuck). SIGNALS: 2 FREQUENCY BANDS — L5 (1176.45 MHz) + S-band (2492.028 MHz). Better multi-path performance than single-frequency. 2 SERVICES: (1) SPS (Standard Positioning Service) — civilian, open; 5m accuracy over land. (2) RS (Restricted Service) — encrypted, military + strategic; few-cm accuracy. GLOBAL COMPETITORS: (1) GPS (USA, 24+3 satellites, global); (2) GLONASS (Russia, 24 operational, global); (3) GALILEO (EU, 30 sat, global); (4) BeiDou (China, 35+ sat, global); (5) QZSS (Japan, 4-7 sat, regional); (6) NavIC (India, 7 sat, regional). GAGAN (GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation) — SEPARATE system; India's SBAS (Satellite Based Augmentation System) — augments GPS signals with corrections for aviation + other precision uses. Launched 2015. USES of NavIC: (a) Terrestrial + marine navigation; (b) Disaster management; (c) Vehicle tracking + fleet management; (d) Mobile phone integration (Android phones with NavIC chips since 2018 — Xiaomi, RealMe); (e) Surveying + mapping; (f) Time synchronisation (telecom, banking); (g) Strategic + defence use. MANDATED for all vehicles (commercial) in India for tracking post-2020. POLICY: Govt mandated NavIC in all new smartphones by ~2023-24 for better indigenous adoption. Successor NVS-01 satellite launched 2023 with Rubidium atomic clocks (indigenous); replaces failed IRNSS-1A.

questions.stem: The ADITYA-L1 mission, India's FIRST SOLAR OBSERVATORY, is parked at:

options.option_text: LAGRANGE POINT L1 (1.5 million km from Earth towards Sun) — halo orbit; uninterrupted view of Sun; reached 6 Jan 2024

questions.explanation: ADITYA-L1 (Sanskrit 'Aditya' = Sun; L1 = Lagrange Point 1) — INDIA'S FIRST DEDICATED SOLAR MISSION. LAUNCHED 2 SEPTEMBER 2023 from Sriharikota on PSLV-C57. REACHED L1 Halo Orbit 6 JANUARY 2024. LAGRANGE POINT L1 — a point ~1.5 MILLION KM from Earth (about 1% of Earth-Sun distance) along the Earth-Sun line where the gravitational pull of Sun + Earth BALANCE with the centrifugal force on a third small body. 5 Lagrange points (L1-L5) exist for any 2-body system. L1 allows UNINTERRUPTED observation of SUN (no eclipse by Earth) + continuous solar wind monitoring BEFORE it reaches Earth — 1-hour early warning of solar storms (coronal mass ejections, CMEs). STATION-KEEPING: halo orbit around L1 (not fixed at L1 itself; L1 is unstable, needs periodic thruster firing). SCIENTIFIC INSTRUMENTS (7 payloads): (1) VELC (Visible Emission Line Coronagraph) — images corona, India-developed by IIA (Indian Institute of Astrophysics, Bengaluru). Key instrument. (2) SUIT (Solar UV Imaging Telescope). (3) SoLEXS (Soft X-ray Spectrometer). (4) HEL1OS (High Energy L1 Orbiting Spectrometer). (5) ASPEX (Aditya Solar wind Particle Experiment). (6) PAPA (Plasma Analyzer Package for Aditya). (7) MAG (MAGnetometer). OBJECTIVES: (a) Study of chromosphere + corona; (b) CME initiation + propagation; (c) solar wind origin + composition; (d) solar flares; (e) corona heating paradox (why corona at millions of Kelvin is hotter than surface at 5800 K?). DESIGN LIFE: 5+ years. OTHER L1 MISSIONS (world): (1) SOHO (Solar + Heliospheric Observatory, NASA-ESA 1995-; still operational); (2) DSCOVR (NASA 2015, Deep Space Climate Observatory — replaces Triana; at L1 monitoring Earth + space weather); (3) ACE (Advanced Composition Explorer, NASA 1997-). OTHER LAGRANGE POINT MISSIONS: JWST (NASA) at L2 (1.5 million km opposite direction). L4 + L5 host 'trojan' asteroids (Sun-Jupiter trojans). SIGNIFICANCE for INDIA: (a) FIRST solar mission; (b) demonstrates INTERPLANETARY capability (after MOM 2013); (c) joins elite 'L1 club' of space agencies; (d) crucial solar + space weather data for India + global science. CHAIRMAN when launched: S. SOMANATH. MISSION OPERATIONS Centre at ISTRAC Bengaluru.

questions.stem: The RAKESH SHARMA became the FIRST Indian in space on:

options.option_text: 3 April 1984 aboard Soyuz T-11 from Baikonur; described India as 'Saare Jahan Se Achcha' to PM Indira Gandhi

questions.explanation: RAKESH SHARMA (b. 13 Jan 1949, Patiala, Punjab) — FIRST INDIAN IN SPACE. IAF Squadron Leader (test pilot, ex-MiG-21). SELECTED 1982 from shortlist of IAF pilots under Indo-Soviet Intercosmos programme; trained at Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre, Star City (Moscow). MISSION: SOYUZ T-11 launched 3 APRIL 1984 from BAIKONUR COSMODROME (Kazakhstan, USSR); docked with SALYUT-7 SPACE STATION on 4 April. Spent 7 DAYS, 21 HOURS, 40 MINUTES in space; returned 11 April 1984 via Soyuz T-10. CREWMATES: Soviet cosmonauts Yuri Malyshev (Commander) + Gennady Strekalov. EXPERIMENTS: (1) Bio-medical experiments on YOGA in microgravity — Rakesh Sharma performed yoga to study muscle efficacy; confirmed yoga's utility. (2) Remote sensing of Indian Himalayan region (10 sites). (3) Metallurgical experiments on silicon + multi-layer melting. (4) Photography of sub-continent. FAMOUS MOMENT: On 5 April 1984, during in-flight conference with PM Indira Gandhi: 'Apki nazar se India kaisa dikhta hai?' ('How does India look from up there?'); Rakesh replied 'SAARE JAHAN SE ACHCHHA' (quote from Iqbal's 1904 patriotic song — 'Better than the entire world'). Iconic line resonates to this day. HONOURS: HERO OF SOVIET UNION (Russia's highest military honor — 1984); ASHOK CHAKRA (India's highest peacetime military award). INDIA became 14TH country to put a person in space (USSR, USA, Czechoslovakia, Poland, E. Germany, Bulgaria, Hungary, Vietnam, Cuba, Mongolia, Romania, France, Germany-W had gone before; India was 14th via Intercosmos). POST-FLIGHT: continued as IAF test pilot; retired 2001; now settled in Tamil Nadu. KALPANA CHAWLA (Haryana-born, naturalised American) went on NASA's STS-87 Space Shuttle Columbia mission 1997; died aboard STS-107 Columbia re-entry disaster 1 Feb 2003. SUNITA WILLIAMS (Indian origin, American; mother Bonnie, father Deepak Pandya) — went to ISS in 2006 + 2012 (127 + 195 days); 2024 Boeing Starliner 1st crewed test (stranded on ISS due to thruster issues, returning via SpaceX Crew-9 in 2025). Rakesh Sharma remains INDIA's ONLY cosmonaut with Indian rocket-flown designation still pending (Gaganyaan).

questions.stem: The FATHER of INDIAN SPACE PROGRAMME, who founded ISRO, is:

options.option_text: DR. VIKRAM SARABHAI (1919-71) — first ISRO Chairman; established PRL Ahmedabad 1947; TERLS Thumba 1963; 'Space City' Bengaluru named partly for him

questions.explanation: DR VIKRAM SARABHAI (12 Aug 1919 – 30 Dec 1971) — 'FATHER of INDIAN SPACE PROGRAMME'; founder + first chairman of ISRO. BORN Ahmedabad (Sarabhai business family; wife Mrinalini Sarabhai was classical dancer; daughter Mallika Sarabhai dancer + activist). Studied at Gujarat College + CAMBRIDGE (PhD in cosmic ray physics under Sir C.V. Raman). RETURN to India 1947. KEY INSTITUTIONS FOUNDED: (1) PHYSICAL RESEARCH LABORATORY (PRL), Ahmedabad (1947) — India's first research institute for cosmic rays + space physics. (2) ISRO (15 Aug 1969) — superseded INCOSPAR (1962, founded by him as well). (3) THUMBA EQUATORIAL ROCKET LAUNCHING STATION (TERLS), Kerala — 1963 (near Thiruvananthapuram; geomagnetic equator passes through it). (4) INDIAN INSTITUTE OF MANAGEMENT (IIM) AHMEDABAD — 1961 (co-founded with Kasturbhai Lalbhai, first IIM). (5) Nehru Foundation for Development. (6) ATIRA (Ahmedabad Textile Industry's Research Association). (7) Centre for Environmental Planning + Technology (CEPT). (8) PHYSICAL RESEARCH LABORATORY. VISION: Sarabhai famously argued India should NOT spend on ROCKETS while poor — BUT his counter was: 'There is no ambiguity of purpose. We do not have the fantasy of competing with the economically advanced nations... we must be SECOND TO NONE in the application of advanced technologies to the real problems of man + society.' Championed SATELLITE TELEVISION for education + rural broadcasting — led to the SITE experiment (Satellite Instructional Television Experiment 1975-76 with NASA's ATS-6, covering 2,400 villages). PROJECTS initiated: Aryabhata satellite, SLV-3 rocket (guided Dr. Kalam's development), ISRO-NASA cooperation, INSAT concept. SUCCEEDED Dr. Homi Bhabha as Chairman of AEC (1966) after Bhabha's death in a plane crash — also oversaw Atomic Energy. DIED 30 DEC 1971 at Kovalam, Kerala (unexpected sudden death, aged 52). Sarabhai was PADMA BHUSHAN 1966; PADMA VIBHUSHAN 1972 (posthumous). ICBM-scale impact on Indian science. VIKRAM LANDER of Chandrayaan-2 + 3 named after him. VSSC (Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre), Trivandrum (ISRO's rocket development centre) named after him. SUCCESSORS: (1) M.G.K. Menon (1971-72); (2) Prof. SATISH DHAWAN (1972-84) — built ISRO into professional organisation; SHAR renamed after him. (3) Prof. U.R. Rao (1984-94). (4) Dr. K. Kasturirangan (1994-2003). (5) G. Madhavan Nair (2003-09). (6) K. Radhakrishnan (2009-14). (7) A.S. Kiran Kumar (2015-18). (8) K. Sivan (2018-22). (9) S. Somanath (2022-).
